theme: Living hope; the church as new Israel; holy living
readingInstruction: Read 1 Peter 1:1-2:12. Peter writes to scattered Christians who suffer for their faith. Notice how he moves from the great things God has done (a living hope, a precious inheritance) to a call to holiness, and then to a new identity as God’s people.
settingTheScene: The apostle Peter wrote this letter around AD 62 to 64, probably from Rome (called “Babylon” in 5:13), to believers in the northern provinces of Asia Minor. Most were Gentiles, though Peter speaks to them in language drawn from Israel. They were “elect exiles,” strangers in a hostile culture, and they faced slander and growing persecution. Peter, who once denied his Lord, writes with the gentleness of a restored man to encourage them to hope.
observation: “He has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead” (1:3).
“You also be holy in all your conduct” (1:15).
“With the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot” (1:19).
“Since you have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God” (1:23).
“You yourselves like living stones are being built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood” (2:5).
“But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession” (2:9).
“Keep your conduct among the Gentiles honorable, so that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day of visitation” (2:12).
interpretation:
Peter greets his readers as “elect exiles of the Dispersion,” chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and for sprinkling with his blood. The Trinity is present from the first verse. Then he bursts into praise: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! According to his great mercy, he has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you, who by God’s power are being guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.” Our hope is alive because Christ is alive, our inheritance is kept safe, and we are kept safe for it.

In this they rejoice, though they now suffer various trials, “so that the tested genuineness of your faith, more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.” Though they have not seen Christ, they love him, and they rejoice with joy that is inexpressible and filled with glory. The prophets searched and inquired about this salvation; angels long to look into these things.

From this foundation, Peter calls for holiness. “Therefore, preparing your minds for action, and being sober-minded, set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.” Do not conform to the passions of your former ignorance, “but as he who called you is holy, you also be holy in all your conduct, since it is written, You shall be holy, for I am holy.” They were ransomed “not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot.” He was foreknown before the foundation of the world but made manifest in the last times for their sake. The new birth is by “the living and abiding word of God.” Love one another earnestly from a pure heart. “The grass withers, and the flower falls, but the word of the Lord remains forever.” That word is the good news that was preached.

Chapter 2 begins with putting away malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander, and craving “pure spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up into salvation.” Christ is the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight. Believers, too, are “living stones” being built up as a spiritual house, “to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.” Peter applies Old Testament texts about the stone: to those who believe, he is precious; to those who do not, he is a stone of stumbling.

Then the great statement of identity: “But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light. Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.” These phrases were used of Israel at Sinai (Exodus 19:5-6) and now belong to the church, made up of Jew and Gentile. This fits the progressive covenantal view that the church is the new covenant people of God, not a replacement but the fulfillment of Israel’s calling in Christ. The purpose is mission: to proclaim his excellencies. As “sojourners and exiles,” they are to abstain from the passions of the flesh and keep their conduct honorable, so that their good deeds may lead even their accusers to glorify God.
connection: Ephesians 1:3-14 is a similar burst of praise. John 3:3-8 and Titus 3:5 speak of new birth. Isaiah 40:6-8 is quoted in 1:24-25. Leviticus 11:44-45 and 19:2 are the source for “be holy.” Isaiah 53 stands behind the lamb. Exodus 19:5-6 is the origin of “kingdom of priests, a holy nation.” Hosea 1:6-10 and 2:23 are behind 2:10. Psalm 118:22 and Isaiah 28:16 are the stone texts. Revelation 1:6 and 5:10 speak of a kingdom and priests. Matthew 5:16 also speaks of good works that glorify the Father. Hebrews 11:13 calls believers strangers and exiles.
application:
Praise God for your living hope before you do anything else today. Read 1:3-5 aloud.

Think about the phrase “chosen race, royal priesthood, holy nation, people for his own possession.” How does it change how you see yourself?

Choose one way to live honorably before a neighbor or coworker who is critical of your faith.
prayerPrompts: Bless God for causing you to be born again to a living hope.
Thank him for keeping an inheritance for you.
Ask him to help you live as a stranger and exile who is holy.
